From 94560267d6c41b1ff3fafbab726e3f8a55a6af34 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Antonio Quartulli <antonio@openvpn.net>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 22:31:19 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] ovpn: tcp - don't deref NULL sk_socket member after
 tcp_close()

When deleting a peer in case of keepalive expiration, the peer is
removed from the OpenVPN hashtable and is temporary inserted in a
"release list" for further processing.

This happens in:
ovpn_peer_keepalive_work()
  unlock_ovpn(release_list)

This processing includes detaching from the socket being used to
talk to this peer, by restoring its original proto and socket
ops/callbacks.

In case of TCP it may happen that, while the peer is sitting in
the release list, userspace decides to close the socket.
This will result in a concurrent execution of:

tcp_close(sk)
  __tcp_close(sk)
    sock_orphan(sk)
      sk_set_socket(sk, NULL)

The last function call will set sk->sk_socket to NULL.

When the releasing routine is resumed, ovpn_tcp_socket_detach()
will attempt to dereference sk->sk_socket to restore its original
ops member. This operation will crash due to sk->sk_socket being NULL.

Fix this race condition by testing-and-accessing
sk->sk_socket atomically under sk->sk_callback_lock.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/netdev/176996279620.3109699.15382994681575380467@eldamar.lan/
Link: https://github.com/OpenVPN/ovpn-net-next/issues/29
Signed-off-by: Antonio Quartulli <antonio@openvpn.net>
Fixes: 11851cbd60ea ("ovpn: implement TCP transport")
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260212213130.11497-1-antonio@openvpn.net
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ovpn/tcp.c b/drivers/net/ovpn/tcp.c
index f0b4e07ba924..ec2bbc28c196 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ovpn/tcp.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ovpn/tcp.c
@@ -199,7 +199,19 @@ void ovpn_tcp_socket_detach(struct ovpn_socket *ovpn_sock)
 	sk->sk_data_ready = peer->tcp.sk_cb.sk_data_ready;
 	sk->sk_write_space = peer->tcp.sk_cb.sk_write_space;
 	sk->sk_prot = peer->tcp.sk_cb.prot;
-	sk->sk_socket->ops = peer->tcp.sk_cb.ops;
+
+	/* tcp_close() may race this function and could set
+	 * sk->sk_socket to NULL. It does so by invoking
+	 * sock_orphan(), which holds sk_callback_lock before
+	 * doing the assignment.
+	 *
+	 * For this reason we acquire the same lock to avoid
+	 * sk_socket to disappear under our feet
+	 */
+	write_lock_bh(&sk->sk_callback_lock);
+	if (sk->sk_socket)
+		sk->sk_socket->ops = peer->tcp.sk_cb.ops;
+	write_unlock_bh(&sk->sk_callback_lock);
 
 	rcu_assign_sk_user_data(sk, NULL);
 }
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file to fix a race condition in the OpenVPN TCP transport. Below is a summary of the modifications and their relationships.

## Modifications in `drivers/net/ovpn/tcp.c`

- **Location**: Function `ovpn_tcp_socket_detach()`.
- **Change**: Wrapped the assignment `sk->sk_socket->ops = peer->tcp.sk_cb.ops` inside a `write_lock_bh(&sk->sk_callback_lock)` / `write_unlock_bh` pair, and added a NULL check for `sk->sk_socket` before accessing its `ops` member.
- **Original code**: Unconditionally dereferenced `sk->sk_socket->ops` without any locking or NULL check.
- **New code**:
  ```c
  write_lock_bh(&sk->sk_callback_lock);
  if (sk->sk_socket)
      sk->sk_socket->ops = peer->tcp.sk_cb.ops;
  write_unlock_bh(&sk->sk_callback_lock);
  ```

## Relationships between modifications

- The modification directly addresses the race condition described in the commit message: `tcp_close()` (via `sock_orphan()`) sets `sk->sk_socket` to `NULL` while holding the same `sk_callback_lock`. Without the lock, the detached function could read a stale non-NULL `sk->sk_socket` pointer and then crash because it becomes `NULL` before the `ops` assignment.
- By acquiring `sk_callback_lock`, the patch ensures that the check `if (sk->sk_socket)` and the subsequent assignment happen atomically with respect to any concurrent `tcp_close()` call. This prevents the NULL-pointer dereference.
- The change is minimal and focused only on the vulnerable code path, preserving the original logic when `sk->sk_socket` is valid.

Here is the root cause:
A race condition occurs when ovpn_tcp_socket_detach() dereferences sk->sk_socket without acquiring sk_callback_lock, while tcp_close() concurrently sets sk->sk_socket to NULL under the same lock via sock_orphan(), causing a NULL pointer dereference.

Here is the patch:
 
 void ovpn_tcp_socket_detach(struct ovpn_socket *ovpn_sock)
 {
 	struct ovpn_peer *peer = ovpn_sock->peer;
 	struct sock *sk = ovpn_sock->sk;
 
 	strp_stop(&peer->tcp.strp);
 	skb_queue_purge(&peer->tcp.user_queue);
 
 	/* restore CBs that were saved in ovpn_sock_set_tcp_cb() */
 	sk->sk_data_ready = peer->tcp.sk_cb.sk_data_ready;
 	sk->sk_write_space = peer->tcp.sk_cb.sk_write_space;
 	sk->sk_prot = peer->tcp.sk_cb.prot;
-	sk->sk_socket->ops = peer->tcp.sk_cb.ops;
+
+	/* tcp_close() may race this function and could set
+	 * sk->sk_socket to NULL. It does so by invoking
+	 * sock_orphan(), which holds sk_callback_lock before
+	 * doing the assignment.
+	 *
+	 * For this reason we acquire the same lock to avoid
+	 * sk_socket to disappear under our feet
+	 */
+	write_lock_bh(&sk->sk_callback_lock);
+	if (sk->sk_socket)
+		sk->sk_socket->ops = peer->tcp.sk_cb.ops;
+	write_unlock_bh(&sk->sk_callback_lock);
 
 	rcu_assign_sk_user_data(sk, NULL);
 }

Reason:
A race condition exists between `ovpn_tcp_socket_detach` and `tcp_close`. The former dereferences `sk->sk_socket` without holding `sk_callback_lock`, while `tcp_close` sets `sk->sk_socket` to `NULL` under the same lock via `sock_orphan`. This allows a concurrent `NULL` pointer dereference, causing a crash.

The code statements that fix the bug are:

`if (sk->sk_socket)`
`	sk->sk_socket->ops = peer->tcp.sk_cb.ops;`
